translationRepairs: (A Dai stele, the 《Stele of Lord Li, Late Tang Longwu Commander, Acting Minister of Works, Posthumously Grand Guardian of Longxi》, records his taboo name Guochang and style Dexing.)〉
(A Dai stele, the 《Stele of Lord Li, Late Tang Longwu Commander, Acting Minister of Works, Posthumously Grand Guardian of Longxi》, records: the lord's taboo name was Guochang, style Dexing.)〉
The stele explicitly gives Li Guochang's taboo name and courtesy name.
Once Wuhuang secured Taiyuan he had him appointed military commissioner of the northern campaign.
When Wuhuang held Taiyuan he memorialized Guochang as military commissioner of the northern Dai army.
表 records Wuhuang's memorial, and 代北軍 is the Northern Dai Army.
He swept Wei and Shuo, raised three thousand men, and camped at New City on Shenwu River.
Wuhuang swept Wei and Shuo, raised three thousand men, and camped at New City on Shenwu River.
武皇 is the explicit subject of the sentence.
In the twelfth month he reached Hezhong.
In the twelfth month Wuhuang reached Hezhong.
武皇 is the stated subject.
He paused in the suburbs, then went to Yanmen to pay his respects at the tomb of his ancestor Xian.
He paused in the suburbs, then went to Yanmen to pay respects to Ancestor Xian.
寧覲 means to pay a respectful visit; the source does not say this was a tomb visit.

Guo Jingyin put out the lamps, steadied Wuhuang, wrapped him in bedding, hid him beneath the couch, splashed water on his face, and whispered: "The Bian commander means to murder you, Minister of Works!"

Guo Jingzhu put out the lamps, steadied Wuhuang, wrapped him in bedding, hid him beneath the couch, splashed water on his face, and whispered: "The Bian commander means to murder you, Minister of Works!"
銖 is read zhū, not yín.
he crossed the river from Heyang and marched on Ru and Luo.
Wuhuang crossed the river from Hezhong and marched on Ru and Luo.
河中 is Hezhong, and the subject remains Wuhuang.
Fangli called on Zhenzhou for help; thirty thousand men came to his aid and Kexiu withdrew.
Meng Fangli called on Zhenzhou for help; thirty thousand men came to his aid and Kexiu withdrew.
The source names Meng Fangli, notwithstanding the graph variant 盂 in this sentence.

Zhu Youyu of Bian encamped at Jin and Jiang; Bian already held Lu, and Li Dan and others were hurrying tens of thousands against Ze; Wuhuang sent Li Cunxiao from Lu with three thousand horsemen to relieve the city.

Zhu Youyu of Bian encamped at Jin and Jiang; Bian already held Lu, and Li Dang and others were hurrying tens of thousands against Ze; Wuhuang sent Li Cunxiao from Lu with three thousand horsemen to relieve the city.

In the fourth month Wuhuang raised a great army against Helian Tuo at Yunzhou, sent the cavalry commander Xue Atan with the vanguard to press the attack, and set ambushers along the Yu River; he broke Tuo utterly and then walled the city in.

In the fourth month Wuhuang raised a great army against Helian Duo at Yunzhou, sent the cavalry commander Xue Atan with the vanguard to press the attack, and set ambushers along the Yu River; he broke Duo utterly and then walled the city in.
In the seventh month Wuhuang advanced to Liuhui; Helian Tuo, out of strength and food, fled to the Tuyuhun and then to Youzhou; Yunzhou was pacified.
